info.title: Yellowcard B2B Payments API
info.description:
B2B Payments API for payments, collections, settlements, currency conversion and custody.

## Authentication
Every request must be signed with your API key using the `YcHmacV1` scheme.

Send two headers:
- `X-YC-Timestamp`: current time as an ISO-8601 string (must be within 5 minutes of server time).
- `Authorization`: `YcHmacV1 <apiKeyId>:<signature>`.

The signature is a base64 HMAC-SHA256 over the message `timestamp + path + method`, and for `POST`/`PUT` requests with a body, `+ base64(sha256(rawBody))` is appended. The HMAC secret is your API key secret.

## Amounts, currencies and rates
USD is the API base currency: `amount` fields are USD, while `convertedAmount` and `*Local` fields are in the local currency. `rate` is expressed as local-currency units per 1 USD (e.g. 1600 NGN/USD). Supported fiat currencies include NGN, KES, GHS, ZAR, UGX, TZS, ZMW, MXN, ARS, BRL and COP; supported custody stablecoins include USDT, USDC, PYUSD and EURC.

rampType.description: deposit = collection (money in); withdraw = payment (money out).

post.description:
Creates a payout to a bank or mobile-money recipient. Supply either `amount` (USD) or `localAmount`; the channel is resolved from `country`, `currency` and `channelType` when `channelId` is omitted. Unless `forceAccept` is set, the payment starts in `pending_approval` and must be accepted.

The Asia corridors require extra recipient details on top of the standard fields. All five — Indonesia (ID/IDR), India (IN/INR), Philippines (PH/PHP), Thailand (TH/THB) and Sri Lanka (LK/LKR) — require `destination.city`, `destination.address`, `destination.idType`, `destination.idNumber`, `destination.occupation` and `purposeOfRemittance`. Per corridor, in addition to those:

- **Indonesia (ID/IDR)** and **Thailand (TH/THB)**: no further fields.
- **India (IN/INR)**: `destination.swiftCode` (the IFSC code).
- **Philippines (PH/PHP)**: `destination.state` and `destination.postalCode`.
- **Sri Lanka (LK/LKR)**: `destination.swiftCode` (the bank branch code).

post.description:
Creates a custody vault to hold crypto assets under the partner.

**Assign one vault per end user.** On non-UTXO chains and tag/memo-based tokens (e.g. EVM, TRON, XRP, XLM) every asset and deposit address in a vault shares a single owner, so a vault cannot be safely shared across users. Dedicate each vault to one user or legal entity and persist the `vaultId` → user mapping on your side: Yellowcard attributes on-chain activity by vault, and travel-rule KYC lookups resolve the vault owner through your registered callback endpoint (see Create or update callback configuration).

**Vaults back direct settlement.** On a disbursement with `directSettlement` set, the crypto leg is debited from the vault named in `settlementInfo.sourceVaultId` instead of the partner fiat balance. On a collection with `directSettlement` set, the collected value settles as crypto into the vault named in `settlementInfo.destinationVaultId` (`internalVault: true`).

post.description:
Registers or updates the custody callback endpoint and its API key. Yellowcard calls this endpoint to fetch the KYC identity of a vault owner on demand, for travel-rule reporting.

**How it works.** When Yellowcard needs the owner of a vault (e.g. for a travel-rule transfer) it resolves the vault to your partner account and sends a signed `POST` to your registered `endpoint` with the vault identifier:

```json
{ "vaultId": "330d2479-61a4-4277-8a30-7063c1587d17" }
```

The request carries `X-YC-Signature` (a base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the secret of the API key registered as `apiKey`) and `X-YC-API-Key` (that key's ID). Verify the signature, resolve which of your users owns that vault, and respond with their KYC identity:

```json
{ "firstname": "Ada", "lastname": "Obi", "country": "NG" }
```

Because the lookup is keyed by vault, each vault must belong to a single user or entity (see Create a vault and Generate a deposit address) and you must maintain the `vaultId` → user mapping to answer these callbacks. Memo/tag-based and UTXO vaults (a single vault with multiple tags or addresses) are not yet supported.
